# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 1, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 16 and nothing else. It read
the ticket, all sixteen records and the seventeen files of the focus set, plus
`docs/harness/reports/calibration.md` and four modules the focus set did not
name (`harness/kpi.py`, `harness/journal.py`, `harness/delivery.py`,
`harness/paths.py`): reading more than the focus set is never refused.

Verdict: **return**, on F1 alone.

`reviewer_session` came back null. A Claude Code subagent inherits its parent's
session id, so the value it could have declared would have been this session's,
which is the session that wrote the work. It is recorded as null rather than
filled with a number that would have read as independence nobody has.

## The findings

**F1, high, `harness/calibration.py:58`.** `path_of` mangles any path starting
with a dot directory and any absolute path, so a high or blocking finding in
such a file is silently counted as no escape rather than as an escape or as
unattributable. `str.lstrip('./')` strips the characters `.` and `/` rather
than the prefix `./`, so `.claude/agents/seen-reviewer.md` becomes
`claude/agents/seen-reviewer.md` while `would_exclude` holds the raw path; the
membership test fails, and because the path is not None no unattributable row
is written either. This ticket's own triage record 16 lists four dot-directory
files in `would_exclude`. Verified against the module's own fixtures: the same
fixture returns one escape for `harness/cli.py` and an empty pair for
`.claude/agents/seen-reviewer.md` and for an absolute path.

**F2, medium, `harness/tests/test_calibration.py:418`.** The only test for the
weekly report's shadow line exercises the branch that cannot see an escape: it
plants an escape but never sets `triage_shadow` to false, so `effective_shadow`
returns at its first branch and the escape sentence is never rendered. Deleting
the escape branch leaves the test green.

**F3, medium, `harness/cli.py:742`.** `harness return --unmet` has no test of
its own; every criterion-escape test plants a record that already carries
`unmet_criteria`. Removing the flag and the field leaves the whole suite green
while the second escape kind becomes permanently undetectable.

**F4, medium, `harness/calibration.py:114`.** A review return that names no
criterion is counted as clean rather than as unattributable, which is the
silent pass the recorded rule says must never happen. Nothing requires the
flag, so an operator who forgets it hides an escape.

**F5, low, `harness/calibration.py:92`.** After go-live the first escape kind is
nearly undetectable, because a spot reviewer never reads the files a kind-one
escape must be found in, and an escaped defect is computed per ticket but is
never an escape. The reviewer names this a scope question for the founder
rather than a coding error: it follows the ticket's own two-kind definition.

## The deterministic checks it was handed

`slice_files` failed at triage and the reviewer passed it: the change to
`harness/tests/test_context_budget.py` is in scope and disclosed, because
SEEN-108 left a guard there asserting `report --calibration` is not a command
the parser accepts, with a note saying the ticket that lands it may lose the
tense. `red_before_green` and `tests_added` came back partial, both naming F2
and F3 and one further gap: slice 1 predicted two REDs and only one is
recorded, the ImportError at record 7; the review gate accepting a blocking
finding with no file was proved by the diff rather than by a check.
`pull_request` stayed unavailable.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

The triage would have excluded 13 of 17 files, 53.08 per cent of the diff. The
one high finding, F1, lands in `harness/calibration.py`, which the triage kept,
and F2 lands in `harness/tests/test_calibration.py`, also kept. Neither is an
escape by the rule, and the four medium and low findings cannot be escapes by
definition. The round therefore reads clean, which is what a shadow window is
for: this ticket is excluded from the window by name in any case.
